title: Upper tail bound for successful blocks
statement: Let $q,K\in\mathbb N$, let $B$ assign a Boolean value to each Boolean word, and let $\varepsilon\in\mathbb Q$ satisfy $0\le\varepsilon$. Suppose that for a uniformly random Boolean word of length $q$, the probability that $B$ is true is at most $1/2-\varepsilon$. For a uniformly random word of length $Kq$, divide it into $K$ consecutive blocks of length $q$, and let $N$ count the blocks on which $B$ is true. Then the probability that $N\ge K/2$ is at most $2(1-4\varepsilon^2)^{\lfloor K/2\rfloor}$.
hypotheses_covered: $B$ maps Boolean words to Boolean values
